newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso closes weak in jittery market.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso closes weak in jittery market.

text.p: The Philippine peso closed lower on Monday as banks continued to be wary of continued currency volatility in the region, traders said.
It ended at 28.479 to the dollar, down from the previous close of 28.47 but up from the day-high of 28.50 as the Manila central bank influenced the market through its dollar sales.
"The big news is that the central bank sold dollars without limit," a trader said.
Traders estimate the central bank may have sold up to $70 million at 28.50/28.45, which resulted to a higher market volume of $114.8 million from $13.6 million.
"Hopefully, the rate will settle down with the central bank's aggressive intervention. Demand for dollars from importers built up over a week ago when supply was still limited," a trader said.

Bankers Association of the Philippines president Deogracias Vistan told Reuters earlier measures adopted by the central bank would eventually encourage exporters and dollar depositors to sell their dollars and ease the pressure on the peso.
The central bank had agreed to sell dollar forward contracts to onshore banks.
Foreign banks, with large dollar demand, had also been requested to stay away from the spot market, Vistan said.
The central bank on Monday also said it will lower its overnight borrowing rate to 22 percent from 25 percent, the third cut in two weeks since the peso's de facto devaluation.
It also raised the liquidity reserve of banks to three percent from two percent to mop up excess liquidity.
